summary: Lay N already-rendered tiles into one labelled contact sheet: a grid of cells at a fixed geometry, each tile optionally composited onto a backplate whose tone is picked from the artwork's own luminance, with literal caption lines drawn under it and a header line across the top. Grid geometry and already-rendered strings in, one picture out. This is the picture a vision judge looks at, and it is the reason the last media exception existed: a URL can only be handed for an object already in the bus, and a sheet composed beside the caller never is.

parity.note: PIL draws deterministically: the layout is integer arithmetic over (grid params, tile count), the plate tone is a pure function of the tile's own alpha-weighted mean luminance, and the glyphs come from one pinned face (fonts-dejavu-core, in the image). Over the same tile bytes the two transports write the same PNG — tests/test_op_media_sheet.py pins that as sha256 against the composite this op replaced, so a layout drift shows as a hash diff instead of as a different picture in front of a judge. THE TOLERANCE, stated because a sheet is SEEN: identical FreeType and zlib give byte-identical files; across Pillow major versions the compressor may repack the same raster, so the floor the parity claim actually stands on is PIXEL identity (RMSE 0), asserted alongside the hash. FAILURE IS PER CELL: an unbound or unreadable tile port leaves its cell empty and every sibling still ships — one chain carries a whole batch of candidates. `sheet` is NOT optional: a caller with no sheet has nothing to judge, and that is an error, not a quiet hold. `meta` is not optional either and it is the half that matters off-box: an empty cell and a rendered one are the same file to a caller that may never look at the pixels, so `drawn` names the cells that actually carry art and a fetch failure keeps its name without a byte of the picture coming back.

cols.description: Cells per row. GEOMETRY: the ORDER the cells are filled in is the caller's, already collapsed into the `captions` array, and no rule that produced that order may appear here.

cell_h.description: Cell height in pixels — also the target height under fit=height.

gap.description: Pixels between cells, and the left margin.

head.description: Header band height above the first row.

caption_h.description: Caption band height under each cell.

line_pitch.description: Default vertical step between caption lines, used for any line that names no explicit `dy`.

fit.description: How a tile meets its cell. `as_is` pastes the tile at its own size (it was rendered to the cell already); `height` scales it to the cell height keeping aspect, clamped to the cell width, which is what lets one grid mix a 3-frame filmstrip with a single still. Geometry, not intent.

plate.description: Composite a see-through tile onto a backplate whose tone is picked from the artwork's own alpha-weighted mean luminance, exactly as media.still picks it. A pixel CONDITION, never an editorial rule: dropping alpha onto black erases a dark mark and pinning it to white erases a light one, and either way the cell reads as empty.

bg.description: Sheet background as [r, g, b]. A brand-adjacent fact resolved on the origin: the pod carries no brand profile, so a colour it had to look up would be missing or wrong there while looking right on the dev box.

header.description: The one line across the top. `text` is ALREADY RENDERED — what it says about the candidates was decided upstream and crosses as a string.

rgb.description: The brand accent, resolved on the origin (brand.rgb) and sent as three integers.

captions.description: One entry per CELL, in cell order, parallel to the tile0..tile23 ports. Its LENGTH is the number of cells — there is no separate count, and a second source for it would be a drift surface. Every string is already rendered: an id, a source name, a resolution, a motion label. NOTHING here may carry a score, a threshold or a sort key; the ranking that produced this order ran on the brain and does not cross.

dy.description: Baseline offset below the cell. Defaults to the line's index times `line_pitch`, plus 3.
